content.text:
In the JusPrin repo (OrcaSlicer fork; read AGENTS.md and agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md first), the MCP server's discovery instructions contradict the server's own behaviour.

Facts, verified on branch jusprin-newui at 198c64606f:
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp`, function `discovery`, builds the MCP `instructions` string from a settings-only paragraph written 2026-09-04 (when the MCP catalogue had five settings tools) plus `Agent::kPrintJourneyGuidance` from `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp`.
- `kPrintJourneyGuidance` says: "For a print request: record the user's explicit purpose as setupTitle with intent_update, even when no setting changes; ...". That sentence was written on 2026-10-06 for the in-app chat's setup card.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` rejects exactly that call from MCP: when `source == ToolSource::Mcp` and `intent_update` arguments contain `setupTitle`, it fails with `chat_title_unavailable` ("A setup title belongs to an in-app chat. MCP can update intent fields only.").
- So every MCP client is instructed to make a call that always fails. The same constant also carries "Ask only the questions whose answer would change what you do", a general behaviour rule for someone else's agent; MCP's own guidance on server instructions (https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-11-03-using-server-instructions/) says to keep instructions to cross-tool relationships, operational patterns and constraints, not to repeat tool descriptions, and not to include general behavioural instructions.

Task:
1. Reproduce first: add or extend a native test (tests/agent/test_mcp_protocol.cpp or test_mcp_runtime.cpp, target `agent_bridge_tests`) showing that the discovery instructions name `setupTitle` while an MCP `intent_update` call with `setupTitle` fails with `chat_title_unavailable`.
2. Give MCP its own short instructions written for an MCP client: the cross-tool patterns that hold for MCP (inspect, preview, apply with the preview's sessionId and revision; re-read after stale_workspace; record requirements as intent fields and the plan with plan_set before changing the project; check slice_report before export_file; closing a response cancels pending work). Do not mention setupTitle, skills, or in-app chat concepts. Cover the current catalogue, not only settings tools.
3. Keep the in-app assistant's prompt behaviour unchanged: the in-app prompt in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` must still carry its print guidance, including the setupTitle sentence. If you split the shared constant, say in a comment which audience each part serves.
4. Update any test that asserts on the old text, build `agent_bridge_tests` (GUI-free; see tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt) and run the whole binary.
Do not commit unless asked. This is a JusPrin-owned area (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/), so no OrcaSlicer-owned files should change.

input.command: git log --oneline -1 && git rev-parse jusprin-newui 2>/dev/null; git merge-base --is-ancestor 198c64606f HEAD && echo "HEAD contains 198c64606f" || echo "HEAD does NOT contain 198c64606f"; git log --oneline HEAD..jusprin-newui | head -20; grep -rn "kPrintJourneyGuidance\|chat_title_unavailable" src tests agent-docs --include=* -r | head -40

1	# Guide for adding JusPrin tools
2	
3	**Status:** Extension guide for the implemented shared registry, embedded MCP server, and stdio bridge. The MCP catalog includes workspace inspection, slice-review reporting, and the settings workflow over the process, one object, and filament and printer presets. A [candidate catalog](#candidate-catalog) derived from the product surfaces follows the implemented catalog record; nothing in it exists unless the catalog record says so.
4	
5	JusPrin has one tool system with multiple adapters. New capabilities are added to the shared registry, executed by `ToolExecutionCoordinator`, and implemented through the typed live-workspace boundary; the OpenAI and MCP adapters only translate that contract to their wire formats. This guide keeps the catalog small, honest, safe to evolve, and driven by real printing tasks rather than an abstract feature inventory.
6	
7	Use this guide as the base, then revise it when implementation evidence, real MCP clients, or evals show that a rule, contract, limit, or sequence should change. Do not preserve a planning assumption merely because it is written here. Keep revisions evidence-based, record substantive changes in the PR, and preserve the product's authoritative ownership and verification requirements.
8	
9	Start with [the production documentation](README.md), [production architecture](architecture.md), and [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) before touching a live Orca owner. Current contracts are defined in [`ToolRegistry.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp), execution in [`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp), and MCP projection in [`McpProtocol.cpp`](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp).
10	
11	For local external clients, use the bundled `jusprin-mcp` stdio helper through **Connect AI tools...**. The helper and native server compile the same registry. Every new exposed tool must therefore have consistent live and offline catalog/schema behavior for the same build and negotiated protocol version; no new adapter-specific catalog is allowed. Direct HTTP is a developer route, not the default setup instruction.
12	
13	## Current connection and execution boundary
14	
15	- The server starts automatically with the JusPrin Agent panel. There is no `JUSPRIN_MCP` enable switch or bearer token. It binds numeric loopback, prefers port 47301, and falls back to an ephemeral port only when that port is occupied.
16	- The shell supplies `<data_dir>/jusprin/mcp.json`. The runtime atomically publishes the actual address, PID, unique runtime `instanceId`, build version and protocol versions. Removal checks the runtime identity under the discovery lock, so an older runtime cannot remove a newer runtime's record, even in the same process. POSIX files use mode `0600`.
17	- The helper validates discovery and probes the endpoint. It follows later app starts/restarts; it never launches JusPrin. A last-writer-wins record supports one selected instance, not an instance chooser. `--discovery`, `JUSPRIN_MCP_DISCOVERY`, and `JUSPRIN_MCP_URL` are explicit path/address overrides, not enable switches; connection entries use `--discovery` for the actual app data directory.
18	- Offline discovery and tool lists come from the compiled registry; offline tool calls return `workspace_unavailable`. With a reachable app, use its live catalog/results, including across version skew; do not substitute the helper's compiled tool list for a different live build. Version skew is logged.
19	- The HTTP adapter accepts protocol `2026-07-28`. The helper additionally negotiates legacy `2025-03-26`, `2025-06-18`, and `2025-11-25`. It handles version projection; tool executors must not implement protocol-specific behavior.
20	- **Connect** confirms the command or file edit before invoking Claude Code/Codex's CLI or merging the JusPrin JSON entry for Claude Desktop/local Cowork, Cursor or VS Code. JSON edits preserve unrelated settings, make a backup, and reject stale previews or symlink destinations. This is not a cross-process transaction against another editor writing at the exact replacement instant.
21	- macOS bundles the helper beside the app executable; Windows has a matching install rule. Linux AppImage entries use the installed image path plus `--mcp-bridge`, dispatched before GUI startup. Do not use a temporary AppImage mount path as the saved command.
22	
23	Native workspace commands run on the GUI thread through the shared coordinator. A shell-owned timer continues execution independently of the WebView handshake. No external client gets direct access to Orca objects.
24	
25	External calls preserve the trusted adapter-assigned `ToolSource::Mcp` for activity history and diagnostics. They execute through the same coordinator and workspace commands as in-app calls.
26	## Start with an eval failure
27	
28	Do not add a tool because Orca has a menu item or config key. Start with a transcript or automated eval where the Agent cannot complete a real user task, completes it unreliably, or consumes unreasonable steps or tokens.
29	
30	Write down:
31	
32	- the user outcome;
33	- the exact point where the current tools become insufficient;
34	- the authoritative Orca state or operation that is missing;
35	- the expected successful transcript;
36	- unsafe or ambiguous cases that must fail; and
37	- the evidence that will show the new contract fixed the problem.
38	
39	If the failure can be fixed by a clearer description, a better result, or a more useful validation error, improve the existing definition instead of adding a tool.
40	
41	The candidate catalog later in this guide is a map, not a licence. A row there does not exempt a tool from this section; it records which product surface and eval family the tool would serve so the eval is easier to write, and it fixes the noun, class, and owner so two people do not build the same capability twice under different names.
42	
43	## Decide whether this should be a tool
44	
45	Add or extend a tool when the Agent needs fresh authoritative state, deterministic computation owned by Orca, or a side effect in the live project.
46	
47	Do not add a tool for:
48	
49	- one setting key; setting keys are records used by generic settings tools;
50	- general printing advice the model can reason about from a skill;
51	- a fixed bundle such as "make it stronger" whose right answer depends on the part and user priorities;
52	- UI automation against a button, widget, or hidden panel;
53	- data already present in a bounded existing result;
54	- speculative future capability with no eval or user task; or
55	- an operation the real adapter cannot perform honestly through an authoritative Orca owner.
56	
57	Deterministic workflow machinery can be a tool. Examples include generating Orca's calibration geometry or starting Orca's slice action. Advice should remain a skill until there is a separately specified deterministic operation behind it.
58	
59	## Skills versus tools
60	
61	A skill is text the model reads. A tool is something the app executes. A candidate is one or the other by one question: does it have to execute (read state the model does not have, compute what only Orca can, change the project), or does it only have to be read (judgement, sequencing, domain facts, how to read a tool's result, which question to ask first)? The section above gives the tool side. This section gives the skill side and rules on the cases that fall between.
62	
63	A skill holds what the model could do with the right knowledge and nothing that executes: judgement over evidence (telling an adhesion failure from wet filament in a photo), the order of a sequence of tool calls and the reasons for it ("make it stronger": read the settings, move walls and infill, slice, read the report), domain facts (what PETG tolerates), and which question to ask when the answer would change the plan. The file-load instructions (`AgentUI/src/fileReportInstructions.ts`) are a skill the app injects for one turn: the first message after a load is judgement over the report, not an operation, so it is text. That is the only kind of skill built so far. A skill the model opens by name, from an index of one line each, has no loader yet; until it does, a skill is text the app injects for the turn whose situation the app knows.
64	
65	The cases between:
66	
67	- **A procedure over existing tools** is a skill while the sequence takes judgement. It becomes a tool only when the sequence is fixed and the person wants it as one undoable action; many such sequences go in one workflow registry (see [When resources or skills are appropriate](#when-resources-or-skills-are-appropriate)).
68	- **An analysis** is a tool when Orca computes it deterministically (overhang angles from geometry) and a skill when it is judgement over evidence, paired with the tool that supplies the evidence (`view_render`, `slice_report`).
69	- **Large reference data** is a tool that returns the part an argument selects (`settings_search`) when the model needs one part of it, and text when the model needs all of it to use any of it. The printer list under [Input design](#input-design) is the measured case where the search tool lost to the whole list in the instructions.
70	- **A tool description** says when to call that one tool, in the words a person would use. **A skill** says how several tools fit together and what to conclude from their results. A description that has grown into a procedure is a skill that has not been split out.
71	
72	When unsure, start as a skill. A skill is a text file the page ships; a tool is the implementation sequence below, with fakes, tests and rebase evidence. Promote a skill to a tool on the evidence every tool starts from (see [Start with an eval failure](#start-with-an-eval-failure)): transcripts show the model getting the sequence wrong in ways text does not fix, or the action needs atomicity, validation or undo only the app can give. The signal from the other side: a skill that has become exact values and ordered calls with no judgement between them is a tool that has not been written yet.
73	
74	Loading does not decide the question. Today a skill costs its line in the instructions and a tool costs its definition on the first request of a conversation (see [Tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)). Under platform deferral both are an index line and a load on demand, and a skill may then be a deferred read-only tool whose description is its index line and whose result is its text, so tools and skills share one discovery mechanism and one eval.
75	
76	## Prefer extending nouns over multiplying verbs
77	
78	The settings workflow uses four stable operations over searchable data, regardless of which preset layer owns the values:
79	
80	```text
81	settings_search → settings_get → settings_preview_patch → settings_apply_patch
82	```
83	
84	Do not create:
85	
86	```text
87	set_layer_height
88	set_wall_loops
89	set_infill_density
90	set_support_angle
91	```
92	
93	The same rule applies to presets, project objects, plates, warnings, and slice reports. Extend their typed record formats and bounded query tools before creating dozens of special-purpose actions.
94	
95	A new verb is justified when it has meaningfully different authorization, atomicity, lifecycle, or result semantics. `slice_start` is not just another settings mutation: it starts asynchronous Orca work and has a different completion contract. That distinction deserves a tool.
96	
97	Use a preview/apply pair only where Orca rewrites, substitutes, or refuses what the caller asked for, so the caller must see the real consequence before proposing it: settings (the normalizer), preset selection (compatibility substitution and lost dirty edits), topology changes (resulting pieces), and preflight (mapping and readiness). Everywhere else the coordinator computes and validates the after-state as part of the call. A preview that would only echo its input is not a tool.
98	
99	Prefer typed reads with fixed schemas over one polymorphic record search. Sections of `workspace_inspect` each keep their own fixed shape; a generic `records_search` whose result shape depends on a `kind` argument makes the model guess.
100	
101	## Tool budget and tool shape
102	
103	Tool count is bounded by what a turn loads, not by what the app can do. The evidence behind these rules: OpenAI's function-calling guidance keeps fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn and defers the rest; Anthropic's [tool-writing guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) asks for a few tools targeting high-impact workflows and names "tools that merely wrap existing software functionality or API endpoints" as the common error; a [domain-oriented MCP study](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.22063v1) measured a generic thin-tool interface below raw SQL and domain-shaped tools far above both; and the "god tool" that dispatches many unrelated actions through one `action` parameter is a documented anti-pattern. The current five-tool MCP catalog measures about 1.9 KB per definition, two thirds of it output schema.
104	
105	- **Loading, for now.** Every registered tool loads on every turn in both adapters: the in-app adapter sends the full function list with each request, and MCP `tools/list` returns the whole catalog. This is the simplest correct behaviour and it keeps the tools array byte-identical across a chat, which is what OpenAI's prompt cache keys on. The budget of 20 definitions per turn is a measured trigger, not a gate: the live regression records definition bytes, input tokens, and cached tokens per request, and the journey catalog below will exceed 20 definitions from its first milestone. That is accepted until those measurements show selection errors or context pressure.
106	- **The baseline, measured on Windows against the live app.** After M5: in-app 25 definitions and 29,148 bytes, MCP 26 and 33,013 over two `tools/list` pages. After M4: in-app 20 definitions and 21,594 bytes, MCP 21 and 24,923 (24,901 through the offline helper recipe). After M3: in-app 20 definitions and 19,331 bytes, MCP 21 and 22,661 (22,639 through the offline helper recipe). After M2: in-app 18 definitions and 12,721 bytes, MCP 16 and 13,911 (13,894 through the offline helper recipe). After M1: in-app 11 definitions and 6,482 bytes, MCP 9 and 6,915. At M0 it was in-app 7 and 3,145 bytes, MCP 5 and 3,147.
107	
108	  The `--live-agent` regression at both points says what that costs. The first request of a conversation caches nothing and pays for the whole catalog: 803 tokens at M0, 1,733 at M1, so four more definitions cost about 930 tokens, once. Every later request in the same conversation came back 77 to 92 per cent cached (5,864 in, 5,376 cached at M1), because the tools array is byte-identical across a chat and that is what the cache keys on. At M2 the same regression's eleven requests took 2,875 to 6,763 input tokens with 42 to 91 per cent cached; none started cold, because an earlier run of the same day had warmed the cache for the shared prefix, so the M2 cold cost is not measured by that run.
109	
110	  So the cost of a definition is what it adds to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn, and the budget stays a trigger rather than a gate. What would change that reading: a catalog large enough to make the first request of every conversation expensive on its own, or transcripts showing the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch both; neither has appeared yet.
111	- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the five printer tools and the four settings tools, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer; the settings tools only with `scope: "printer"` on the printer the conversation is about. A Change conversation may be about the stock profile the project has selected (the header's Printer settings… on a project that uses one); its nozzle and connection are refused with `stock_profile`, and its settings are saved as a copy that the conversation then follows (`PrinterConversation::tool_settled`). A Change conversation is never turned into an Add one: its opener checks that the printer is there and shows Orca's error dialog when it is not. The header's filament chat (the same panel, `PrinterPanel::open_filament`) is offered the four settings tools and nothing else, with no project state, and its own instructions, which the page writes (`AgentUI/src/filamentInstructions.ts`, sent with `filament_instructions`) from the facts the app sends as the state's session (`PrinterPanel::filament_session_json`: the preset by name, its slot and material, and for a stock filament the copy a change is saved as). Its preflight holds the settings tools to `scope: "filament"` on that preset and refuses an apply without `persistAs` (`not_saved`), since the chat is gone when it closes; a copy saved in the preset's place is the preset it is about from then on, and the page writes the instructions again for it. Until 2026-09-29 it ran on the project assistant's instructions and tools, which read "make the nozzle 5 degrees hotter" as a print request, and in another run set 205 °C from 220 °C without reading it. A list that differs by mode is not used: the conversation's own refusal is needed whatever the model is shown, and a restricted-but-stable list (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. What would change that: transcripts of the model reaching for a refused tool and not recovering, which `tests/printer_prompt` measures (`change-add-another`). Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). On 2026-09-28 the three tools that opened a window or closed the panel -- `printer_manual_setup`, `printer_manual_connection` and `printer_setup_finish` -- were removed (b60fc2d8e6): OrcaSlicer's full printer list and a printer's settings stay reachable from the panel's own buttons, and the person closes the panel. The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.
112	- **Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Use the platform's own deferral, never a hand-rolled switcher. On the in-app side that is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API, documented for `gpt-5.4` and later; support on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unverified. On the MCP side clients defer on their own, as Claude Code does. Toolsets are the deferral unit, and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. An enable-toolset tool that rewrites the tools array breaks the prompt cache on every switch and is not to be built.
113	- **Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing a slicer user would name: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Not a wrapper per Orca function, and not an interpreter for a list of unrelated commands. Optional facets of one operation are fine when each is independently typed and conflicting facets are rejected.
114	- **Batch only where items share a shape.** A list of setting changes, a list of intent fields, a list of annotations, a list of per-object layout rows. A list that mixes transforms, imports, and deletes is the god tool and is refused.
115	- **Fold reads into sections and detail levels** before adding a read tool. A new read tool is justified only by a different input contract (a search over a large catalog, a per-object analysis, a sliced-plate report) or an image result.
116	- **Let call logs decide consolidation.** Two tools that transcripts show always called together are candidates to merge; two facets never used together are candidates to split. Consolidation follows evidence from evals, not the whiteboard.
117	- **Output schemas are not advertised over MCP.** No client was shown to use them, and they were two thirds of the catalog. `tools/list` stopped carrying `outputSchema`; `validate_output` still checks every MCP success, so a result that violates its contract still fails loudly. Measured on the same build with the recipe below: five tools, 9,723 bytes before, 3,141 after, about 2,430 tokens down to 785. The saving is MCP-side only: the in-app adapter has always sent `input_schema` as `parameters` and nothing else, so an in-app turn was never carrying them. Restore the field only for a client that is shown to read it.
118	
119	## Choose the narrowest honest scope
120	
121	Never put an enum value such as `printer | filament | process | object` in a schema unless every advertised value works in the fake and real adapter and has the documented inheritance behavior.
122	
123	For each proposed capability, answer:
124	
125	1. Which Orca owner contains the authoritative state or operation?
126	2. Is the command valid for the whole project, one plate, one object, one instance, or one preset layer?
127	3. What stable ID identifies the target, and when does that ID expire?
128	4. What revision must still match when the command executes?
129	5. What existing Orca snapshot and undo/reset/revert behavior encloses it, or does ordinary project Undo not apply?
130	6. Which workspace change reasons announce that readers must refresh?
131	7. What happens if the user edits the GUI while the call is queued or running?
132	
133	If these answers are unclear, the tool contract is not ready.
134	
135	## Reuse the one authority path
136	
137	Every mutation must follow this route:
138	
139	```text
140	adapter call
141	→ shared registry validation
142	→ ToolExecutionCoordinator queue
143	→ immediate execution
144	→ IWorkspace command
145	→ current Orca owner
146	→ Orca history and state change
147	→ coalesced workspace event
148	→ fresh snapshot/result
149	```
150	
151	Do not let an adapter call `Plater`, `Model`, `PresetBundle`, wxWidgets, or slicing objects directly. Do not copy an Orca operation into JusPrin. When a required operation is trapped in presentation code, add the smallest behavior-oriented, product-neutral seam at its current owner.
152	
153	Changes in OrcaSlicer-owned files must satisfy [fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md): keep the diff small and additive, record why the seam belongs there, identify upstream lines touched, and include rebase evidence.
154	
155	## JusPrin-owned project state
156	
157	Some product state has no Orca owner: the print intent, the pinned agent plan, semantic region annotations, physical facts the user confirmed about a printer, and the monitoring policy that authorizes automatic pausing. For these the "current Orca owner" step of the authority path is a JusPrin store; every other step stays. The rules:
158	
159	- **Storage.** Project-scoped state (intent, plan, regions, conversation, and attachments) lives in the local project store under a stable project ID. The current `ProjectStateDocument` is saved independently of model checkpoints; imported legacy `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json` and its recovery mirror are read for migration only. The print intent (`printIntent`, upserted by field name, each with provenance), the plan (`plan`, replaced whole) and the region annotations (`regions`, replaced whole, each record stamped with a seq when it changes) remain fields of that document. Printer-scoped state (confirmed facts, monitoring policy) stays in app data keyed by printer identity, as `PrinterFactsStore` keeps it; confirmed facts carry an expiry because the physical world changes without telling the app. See [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md).
160	- **Revision.** Every write announces itself so readers refresh. Which announcement, and whether it invalidates queued actions, is **open** and belongs to the milestone that lands the first writer. The obvious reading — publish a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` bit and add it to `kInvalidatingReasons` — is not implementable as stated: `settings_apply_patch` compares its caller's `expectedRevision` against the current revision for exact equality, so any revision advance between a client's preview and its apply fails as `stale_workspace`. An agent that records its plan between previewing and applying would break its own call. The edit feed (`WorkspaceEditHub`) is the precedent for a feed that reports a change without advancing the revision. Decide per kind: a region annotation generates Orca artifacts and is a real project change; an intent answer or a plan statement is not. As built, a region record's own write announces nothing; the artifacts it generates are Orca edits and advance the revision the ordinary way, so an action queued before an annotation goes stale exactly as it would after any other model edit.
161	- **Undo.** None of this state is in Orca's undo stack. Results say `projectUndo: false`. Region annotations generate Orca artifacts (modifier volumes, enforcers, blockers, paint) that *are* in the undo stack, so project Undo can strand an annotation without its artifacts or an artifact without its annotation. the `regions` section of `object_analyze` reports both conditions and `region_annotate` regenerates; a place, divide, or repair result lists the regions whose binding it broke.
162	- **Provenance.** Any field that records a fact about the world or the user's wishes carries where it came from: `file` (read from the project or profile), `observed` (a sensor or printer report, with a timestamp), `agent_inferred`, or `user_confirmed`. A tool marks a value `user_confirmed` only when the call is grounded in an explicit user statement; inferred values stay `agent_inferred`. Printer reads distinguish `configured` from `observed` for the same fact and compute `mismatches` between them rather than leaving that to the model.
163	
164	## Define the contract before the implementation
165	
166	Every new tool's registry entry and accompanying contract/tests must specify:
167	
168	- stable lowercase underscore name;
169	- concise title shown in activity UI;
170	- compact description that says when to use the tool;
171	- strict input JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false` where practical;
172	- output JSON Schema;
173	- trusted `ActionClass`;
174	- exposure to the in-app Agent, MCP, or both;
175	- availability requirements, such as an open FFF project or selected object;
176	- whether an action is revision-sensitive;
177	- atomicity and the real undo, reset, or revert behavior (including an explicit statement when normal project Undo does not apply);
178	- cancellation behavior;
179	- bounded output and pagination limits; and
180	- structured domain errors.
181	
182	The registry is immutable and deterministically ordered. Adapters may filter by declared static exposure, but they must not rewrite action class, validation, or behavior. Keep the MCP-visible list stable unless the server also implements and tests the current protocol's tool-list change notification contract; report unmet live preconditions from `tools/call` instead.
183	
184	`ToolDefinition` currently stores name, title, description, input/output schemas, action class, exposure, availability and handler. Revision sensitivity, atomicity, cancellation and history semantics live in the coordinator/workspace implementation and tests, not in additional registry fields. `ToolAvailability` currently describes request context (`Always` or `ImportableAttachment`), not a dynamic project-state filter.
185	
186	Input validation uses the registry's handler-specific `valid_arguments` decoder; changing only JSON Schema does not change accepted calls. MCP success output is checked by `validate_output`, whose schema vocabulary is deliberately limited. Extend that validator with tests before adding unsupported schema keywords. Do not assume it implements all of JSON Schema or that every adapter automatically validates output.
187	
188	### Naming and compatibility
189	
190	- Prefer names such as `slice_start` and `presets_compare`.
191	- Do not rename a released tool casually. Treat names and schemas as public APIs.
192	- Add optional fields compatibly. Do not change the meaning or type of an existing field.
193	- When a breaking contract is unavoidable, add a versioned replacement, stop advertising the old definition after a documented migration window, and keep a focused compatibility test while both exist.
194	- Keep one canonical name across adapters. Do not maintain OpenAI and MCP aliases unless a client defect is documented and tested.

196	## Input design
197	
198	Inputs should express intent and identity, not transport or UI mechanics.
199	
200	- Send Orca IDs as JSON strings to preserve native width.
201	- Use canonical setting keys and normalized values.
202	- The three in-app fixtures of the first catalog (`duplicate_object`, `import_model`, `inspect_selection`) are retired: `plate_layout` replaced the first, `object_import` the second, and the selection ids in `workspace_inspect`'s summary the third. The coordinator captures session/revision when it queues an action, invalidates queued actions on relevant workspace events, and rechecks before executing. Selection-only changes do not redirect or invalidate a pinned object target.
203	- For a new read-modify-write operation that must detect changes since the caller's earlier read, design and test explicit expected-session/revision inputs in its own schema and decoder. Proposal-time checks alone do not prove the caller's earlier read is current; do not retrofit required arguments onto existing tools silently.
204	- Batch changes that must be atomic.
205	- Prefer explicit selectors over magic defaults, except when the name clearly promises the current selection or active plate.
206	- Reject unknown fields and conflicting selectors.
207	- A filesystem path may cross the boundary only through a tool that validates the exact absolute path, constrains its kind and location, and documents whether it reads, creates, or overwrites. The candidate catalog has three such tools: `object_import_file`, `project_open`, and `export_file`. No read-only tool accepts a path. In-app clients keep the attachment route, which needs no path.
208	- Do not make the model repeat data the server can read authoritatively at execution time.
209	- Do not encode a large catalog as a schema enum; use bounded search and detail retrieval.
210	- **One exception, with its evidence: the printer list.** Identifying a printer from what someone says is the model's understanding, not a lookup, and a search tool in front of it did it badly: `printer_catalog_search` required every word of the query in a model's name and returned the first few in file order, so "voron 2.4 350mm" came back unsupported, "x1c" matched another manufacturer's printer and "prusa" showed three of thirteen. The Add session's instructions instead carry every printer the panel offers, one line each (`<catalogId> | <brand> <model> | <build volume>`, 383 lines from `PrinterCatalog::panel_printers`, sent to the page as the session's `context` and written into the instructions by `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), and `printer_identify` checks the ids the model copies from it. Measured 2026-09-18 through the app's own request and tool results on `gpt-5.4-mini`, three runs of each case: the word test set 138/150, the photo test set 29/45, the handoff's own cases (those four queries among them) 21/21. The model tried to show more than three printers 33 times; each was refused with `too_many` and it then asked a narrowing question, so no answer ever showed three of many. The weak spots are a query that equals one model name and begins others ("bambu a1": 0/3) and photos with no readable name. The test sets and the runner are in `agent-docs/jusprin/spikes/printer-identify/` (uncommitted, beside the earlier spikes). The list is a fixed prefix of the instructions, so it caches; it is the right shape only while it stays a few hundred lines.
211	
212	The coordinator resolves the action class and handler from the name. Never accept either from call arguments.

214	## Output design
215	
216	Design response size before adding fields. A full project tree, all setting definitions, per-layer G-code statistics, or unbounded warnings can consume more context than the entire tool catalog.
217	
218	Every read tool should use one or more of:
219	
220	- a concise/default/detail level;
221	- explicit field selection;
222	- pagination with deterministic order;
223	- a hard item limit;
224	- aggregate summaries followed by targeted detail calls; or
225	- an explicit `truncated` flag and continuation cursor.
226	
227	For new live-state contracts, include `sessionId` and `revision` when needed to identify and validate later calls. `workspace_inspect` returns both, with the selection as ids. Internal history-record results have their own schemas. MCP activity results also carry action ID, current session and revision in `_meta["io.jusprin/activity"]`. If an event says state changed, fetch a fresh snapshot; never treat the event itself as the new state.
228	
229	For MCP success, produce schema-valid `structuredContent` and a serialized text block describing the same result. Errors use the shared `{error: {code, message, details}}` envelope with `isError: true`, not the success output schema. The bridge removes modern-only result/cache fields for legacy clients. For `2025-03-26` it also omits `structuredContent` and catalog `outputSchema`/`title`, preserving the serialized text result; later supported revisions retain `structuredContent` and `title`. No negotiated version advertises `outputSchema` any more (see [tool budget and tool shape](#tool-budget-and-tool-shape)); the bridge's own stripping stays because it also projects catalogs forwarded from a live app of another version. These are intentional compatibility projections, not conflicting tool definitions.
230	
231	### Image results
232	
233	Three candidate reads return a picture: `project_attachment_read` (a reference image), `view_render` (the prepared or sliced scene), and `printer_camera_snapshot`. The registry result carries the encoded image plus a structured block describing it (dimensions, camera or layer range, capture time), and each adapter projects that one result:
234	
235	- MCP: an `image` content block beside the text and structured result; on `2025-03-26` the same block, since image content predates structured content.
236	- OpenAI: the text and structured block as the function result, and the image appended as an image input in the continuation, since function results are text-only.
237	
238	This is an adapter projection, not forked behavior. Both projections must be tested before the first image-returning tool ships. Cap every image (1280 pixels on the long edge, 2 MB) so one frame never dominates the context window, and never return an image the user has not allowed: camera frames require the privacy grant in Printer Configuration and otherwise fail with `camera_disabled`.
239	
240	## Errors should teach the next valid call
241	
242	Expected invalid states use structured control flow, not thrown exceptions. An error should identify the problem and provide only the correction data the Agent needs.
243	
244	Current MCP errors include `invalid_arguments`, `cancelled`, `workspace_unavailable` and `stale_workspace`. The MCP adapter normalizes native `stale_revision`/`stale_id` to `stale_workspace` with expected/current session and revision details, and `unavailable_operation` to `workspace_unavailable`. Transport-level protocol errors are separate JSON-RPC errors. Do not require identical spelling across the native and MCP error boundaries.
245	
246	The settings tools implement the following bounded correction details:
247	
248	- unknown setting: canonical `unknown_setting`, original key, and a short `suggestions` list;
249	- invalid enum: key, diagnostic message, and valid values in `allowed`;
250	- out of range: key, diagnostic message, and `min`/`max` bounds; units are available from setting metadata;
251	- incompatible settings: conflicting keys and Orca's reason;
252	- stale call: expected and current session/revision, plus instruction to read again;
253	- unavailable operation: the requested scope has no active preset or target;
254	
255	Unexpected invariant failures must remain visible to diagnostics and Sentry. Catch at an abstraction boundary only to recover, translate a known error, or add essential context.
256	
257	## Read, mutation, and destructive policy
258	
259	Use the registry's action class, not naming conventions:
260	
261	- **Read-only:** cannot alter project, preset, disk, printer, or durable product state.
262	- **Mutation:** changes project, preset, or durable product state.
263	- **Destructive:** may delete, overwrite, discard, print, export, or restore history.
264	
265	Action class remains metadata for UI wording, MCP annotations, staleness checks, and audit history. Valid tool calls start immediately after validation. A tool that previews changes is read-only only if fake and real tests prove it does not dirty presets, advance the workspace revision, create history, cancel slicing, or write files.
266	
267	## Asynchronous operations
268	
269	Use asynchronous behavior only when Orca's real operation is asynchronous. Do not invent a second job engine.
270	
271	For slicing and later long-running actions:
272	
273	1. the workspace command starts work through Orca's current owner and returns a stable action handle;
274	2. `ToolActivity` records running and terminal state with bounded progress;
275	3. Orca completion or failure advances/invalidates authoritative workspace state;
276	4. the consumer fetches the authoritative slice report or error after the event; and
277	5. cancellation calls Orca's real cancellation path and reports whether cancellation won the race.
278	
279	MCP progress notifications are optional request-scoped presentation. They must be monotonic and must not be the only way to learn the terminal result. Add the MCP Tasks extension only when a real client/eval needs durable calls that outlive one request; do not add it merely because an operation takes several seconds.
280	
281	The current coordinator stages execution through GUI ticks; it does not provide durable asynchronous jobs. The bridge accepts `notifications/cancelled` in both protocol eras, closes the forwarded connection, and suppresses subsequent output for that request. EOF ends the bridge session. A lost connection before the final response produces `connection_lost` with an **unknown outcome** warning, not proof the mutation was cancelled. Never automatically retry a mutation after such a loss; inspect authoritative state first.
282	
283	## Tool exposure
284	
285	Default to both adapters when both can satisfy the same input contract. A deliberate filter is appropriate when context is supplied differently:
286	
287	- `workspace_inspect` is exposed to both adapters so either can obtain a fresh completed slice identity after slicing, independently of the initial turn context;
288	- attachment-based import (`object_import`) is in-app-only, and path-based `object_import_file` is MCP-only, because a file reaches the app through the conversation in one case and through an explicit path in the other; that is two honest definitions over one workspace command, not one tool with forked behavior; and
289	- a future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP-only if it exists to establish the external connection; and
290	- the printer panel's five own tools carry only the `Printer` exposure: neither adapter lists them, and the panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses what does not fit it (see "Tool budget and tool shape"). and what the model reads back from them is the tool's own result, not the host's workspace envelope.
291	
292	Document the reason beside the registry definition and test it. Exposure is not a place to fork behavior: if two adapters need different semantics, they need a better shared command or honestly separate definitions.
293	
294	## When resources or skills are appropriate
295	
296	Do not make MCP resources load-bearing until intended clients prove that model-driven resource retrieval is reliable. A bounded data-returning tool is the compatibility baseline. Resources may be added as an optional alternate projection of large, readable, stable data.
297	
298	Keep printing playbooks—reducing stringing, improving strength, choosing support strategy—as skills the model can read (see [Skills versus tools](#skills-versus-tools)). Convert a workflow into an executable tool only when it maps to a named, deterministic Orca operation with defined inputs, outputs, validation, and undo/reset/cancellation behavior. If many procedural workflows eventually qualify, prefer one discoverable workflow registry over dozens of nearly identical tool definitions.

300	## Required implementation sequence for one new tool
301	
302	1. Add or update the failing eval and expected transcript.
303	2. Trace the real Orca owner and record lifecycle, threading, history, and event behavior.
304	3. Define the typed workspace input, output, and error contract.
305	4. Implement the fake adapter and workspace contract tests.
306	5. Implement the real adapter through the smallest owner seam.
307	6. Prove direct GUI edits and tool edits produce equivalent observable state.
308	7. Add the registry definition, decoder/validator, executor association, and output schema.
309	8. Add coordinator tests for action class, staleness, atomicity, cancellation, and terminal activity.
310	9. Add projection tests for every exposed adapter.
311	10. Add protocol fixtures and output-limit tests.
312	11. Run a real-app harness and one end-to-end external-client transcript.
313	12. Update the catalog below and attach verification/rebase evidence to the PR.
314	
315	Do not merge a registry entry backed only by the fake workspace.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.

  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.

  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.

  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in

  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.

description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

MCP clients now get their own short instructions that only describe calls the MCP server accepts; the in-app assistant's prompt is byte-for-byte unchanged. The contradiction was reproduced with a failing test before the fix, and the full native test binary passes after it. Nothing is committed.

## Problem

Reproduced on this worktree (same source as `198c64606f` for these files). Against unchanged source, the new wire test showed the server's discovery instructions containing `setupTitle`, while an MCP `intent_update` call with `setupTitle` on the same server came back `chat_title_unavailable`.

## Solution

- **MCP instructions**: [McpProtocol.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp) has a new `kInstructions` constant, 741 bytes, used by `discovery` and so also by the stdio helper's `initialize`. The text it serves:

  > These tools act on the project open in the running JusPrin app, which the user may be editing at the same time. Read the current state with workspace_inspect before changing it. Where a change has a dry run (settings_preview_patch, printer_setup_preview, object_divide_preview), preview first; settings_apply_patch takes the sessionId and revision its preview returned. A stale_workspace error means the project changed after your read: read and preview again before retrying. For a print request, record the requirements the user stated as intent_update fields, and your plan with plan_set, before changing the project. Check a slice with slice_report before writing its G-code with export_file. Closing a response cancels its pending work.

- **In-app prompt**: `kPrintJourneyGuidance` in [ToolRegistry.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.hpp) keeps its text; only its comment changed, to say it serves the in-app assistant only and where MCP's text lives.
- **Guide**: one paragraph added under "Tool exposure" in [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md). You did not ask for this; drop it if unwanted.

Two things to know about the wording:

- **Revision only for settings**: only `settings_apply_patch` takes a preview's sessionId and revision. `printer_setup` and `object_divide` have previews but no such arguments, so the text says "preview first" for all three and names the revision only for settings.
- **Two old sentences dropped**: "Project Undo does not reverse preset edits" repeats the `settings_apply_patch` description. "`workspace_unavailable` means open JusPrin and a project" is already in the offline error's own message, and the server also uses that code for other conditions such as a project with no plate.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed.

- **Wire test** in [test_mcp_runtime.cpp](tests/agent/test_mcp_runtime.cpp): the `setupTitle` call is refused with `chat_title_unavailable`, the instructions do not name `setupTitle`, and a fields-only `intent_update` succeeds over MCP.

`intent_update` is now off the MCP server, and my earlier connection-note rewrite is gone: you were right that most of it was not necessary. The whole change is now 15 lines added and 30 removed, uncommitted, on top of the merged `jusprin-newui` I just pulled.

## Your two questions

**Should outside agents have `intent_update` at all?** No. I checked what reads the recorded intent: only two read tools (`workspace_inspect` and `slice_report`) and the in-app chat's setup card. An outside agent already holds what its user said in its own conversation, so writing it into JusPrin does nothing for it. Outside agents can still read what the in-app chat recorded.

**Was the connection-note change necessary?** One line of it was. The old note pasted the in-app assistant's print guidance onto the end, and that guidance names `intent_update`, a tool outside agents no longer have. So the paste had to go. The rest (the rewritten note, the three new tests, the guide paragraph) was not necessary, and I reverted it.

## What changed

- **`intent_update`**: in-app only. Its description lost the sentences about MCP callers.
- **Refusal code**: the `chat_title_unavailable` check and its test are deleted, since no outside caller can reach the tool.
- **MCP connection note**: back to the original settings paragraph, without the pasted in-app guidance. It now reads: "Inspect the live workspace, search or read process settings, then preview a patch. Apply with the sessionId and revision from that preview. After stale_workspace, read and preview again. Project Undo does not reverse preset edits; use preset revert or an inverse patch. A workspace_unavailable error means you should open JusPrin and a project. Closing a response cancels pending work."
- **In-app prompt**: unchanged; only the comment on the shared constant now says it is in-app only.
- **Existing tests**: four tests that list or count the MCP tools were updated for one fewer tool.
- **Tool guide**: three small edits to match.

## Results

- Native test binary `agent_bridge_tests`: all 264 test cases pass (4673 assertions).
- Python bridge tests: 18 run, 1 skipped (Linux-only), all pass.
- The rebuilt stdio helper serves the note above and no longer lists `intent_update`.
- Not run: the full app and its shell harness, which call `intent_update` only through the in-app path that this change does not touch.

## One thing for you to decide

The outside note no longer says "record your plan with `plan_set`" or "check `slice_report` before exporting", because those sentences were part of the pasted in-app text. `plan_set` itself is still available to outside agents. The same question applies to it as to `intent_update`: do you want `plan_set` removed from MCP too?

Good point, let's remove plan sets also. In the meantime, we need to make sure that whatever changes external tool mix will be recorded in the history similar to the menu changes being recorded. Can you check the code to make sure of that?

`plan_set` is now off the MCP server too, and I checked the history question by reading the code and by running a probe. Changes made by an outside tool are recorded in the same change log as manual edits, with the same before-and-after values, but the log cannot tell an outside tool from the built-in assistant.

## History check

**How it works.** JusPrin does not record edits per caller. The workspace watches the project itself (undo steps, setting values, preset switches) and writes one change-log entry per edit, whoever made it. While any tool call runs, the entry is stamped "agent"; otherwise "person". Outside tools and the built-in assistant run through that same code path.

**What I ran.** A throwaway test (since deleted) made one manual edit, two edits through the real MCP server, and one through the in-app path, then printed the stored log:

```
kind=setting actor=person label=Wall loops 2->3              (manual edit)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 3->4              (outside tool, process setting)
kind=step    actor=agent  label=Change object settings       (outside tool, undo step)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 4->6              (outside tool, object override)
kind=setting actor=agent  label=Wall loops 4->5              (built-in assistant)
```

The tool-call records stored beside it do say where each call came from: `source=mcp` for the outside tool, `source=agent` for the built-in assistant.

**Gaps I found:**

- **No way to tell who the "Agent" was.** An outside tool's change is stored and displayed as "Agent", identical to the built-in assistant. The page receives the `source` field on tool calls but never uses it.
- **No card for the outside call.** The page only draws a tool call under the chat message that made it. An outside call belongs to no message, so the user sees the change row but not the call.
- **It lands in whatever chat is open.** The change is attached to the active chat even though that chat did not cause it, and that chat's setup card then treats the settings as agent-made.

**Limits of this check.** The probe used the test stand-in for the workspace, not the real app. For the real app I only read the code: edit detection runs inside the tool call, and a version checkpoint is saved before and after any tool change regardless of caller. One case I did not verify: arrange or auto-orient jobs that finish after the tool call returns may be logged as "person".

Changes made by an outside tool are now labelled "External tool" in the history instead of "Agent". All tests pass; nothing is committed, and I have not built or run the full app, only the GUI-free test binary and the page's test suite.

## What changed

- **Recording:** each change-log entry now carries a flag saying it came through the MCP server. The tool runner already knew the caller; it now passes that along when it stamps an edit. The flag is saved with the project and survives a reload. Older saved projects have no flag and read as before.
- **Display:** a flagged row reads, for example, "Wall loops 3 → 4" with "External tool, in Strong · 10:42" underneath, where an in-app change says "Agent" and a manual one says "you".
- **Grouping:** the built-in assistant's setting changes fold into a compact "N settings" block that has no "who" label. External-tool changes are kept out of that block and shown one row per setting, like manual edits, so the label is always visible. An external run also never merges with an adjacent in-app run.

The main edits are in [Workspace.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp), [ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp) and [ChangeRows.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/ChangeRows.tsx).

## What did not change

Everything else still treats an external-tool change as an agent change. In particular the open chat's setup card still counts those settings as agent-made, and the change still lands in whichever chat is open. You asked only for the label, so I left those alone.

## Tests

- **Native** (`agent_bridge_tests`): all 265 test cases pass (4677 assertions). One new test makes a manual edit, an edit through the real MCP server and an in-app edit, reloads the saved project, and checks only the MCP one is flagged.

- The label was checked by the page's rendering tests, not by eye in the running app. "External tool" is longer than "Agent", so the row's second line is worth a glance for wrapping in a narrow panel.
- The full app was not compiled. The shared header I changed is also used by the app's real workspace code; the change keeps the old call form valid, so I expect it to compile, but that is untested.

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Stop offering intent_update and plan_set to MCP clients

The MCP server's connection instructions ended with the in-app assistant's
print guidance, which told every external client to record a setup title
with intent_update. The server always refused that call from MCP
(chat_title_unavailable), because the title belongs to an in-app chat.

The intent record and the pinned plan serve the in-app chat only: its setup
card, and what its user told it. An external agent keeps what its user said,
and its plan, in its own conversation. So:

- intent_update and plan_set are in-app only. MCP clients can still read
  the intent and the plan through workspace_inspect and slice_report.
- The MCP instructions no longer carry the in-app print guidance, which
  names those two tools. The in-app assistant's prompt is unchanged.
- The chat_title_unavailable refusal and its test are removed: no MCP
  caller can reach intent_update any more.

The MCP catalogue goes from 29 tools to 27.
EOF
git add -A agent-docs src tests && git diff --cached --stat | tail -1 && git diff --cached --check && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Label edits made by an external tool in the change log

An edit made through the MCP server was recorded in the change log as the
in-app Agent's, so the thread showed "Agent" for a change that an external
client such as Claude Code made.

The tool coordinator now tells the workspace which caller a command came
from, and a change entry an external tool caused is saved with
"external": true. Its actor stays "agent", so everything that treats agent
edits alike (undo of an agent step, the setup card) behaves as before, and
projects saved earlier load unchanged.

In the thread an external tool's edits read "External tool" where an in-app
change reads "Agent". They are drawn one row per edit, like hand edits, and
are kept out of the in-app Agent's grouped settings block, which has no
room to say who made a change.
EOF
